subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Ransom Olds and Mass Production
description: A short lesson to help you apply Ransom Olds and Mass Production.

hook.text: Henry Ford gets credit for mass-producing cars. Ransom Olds did it first.

buildup.text: The 1901 Curved Dash Oldsmobile was the first car built on a basic assembly line.

discovery.text: Olds sold 425 cars the first year and 5,000 by 1904—numbers no carmaker had ever hit.

twist.text: A factory fire destroyed his plant in 1901. Only the Curved Dash prototype survived.

climax.text: He rebuilt, outsourced parts to local shops, and accidentally invented the supplier model Ford later perfected.

punchline.text: The man who started mass production got forgotten by history.

quiz.question: What was the first mass-produced car?
